content:
This is your sketch, not your statement — but even a sketch this rough tells me something worth acting on.

Your fixed base runs ≈£1,170/mo, which leaves ≈£2,030 free after income. The deposit needs ≈£830/mo — ≈26% of take-home — and that's achievable. The problem is that only ≈£150 in eating out and ≈£250 in saving are accounted for. That leaves ≈£1,630/mo drifting somewhere unexamined.

The move: set up a standing transfer of ≈£300/mo on payday. That's roughly half the drift, so it won't bite. At that pace the deposit lands in ≈37 months. Without it, you're looking at ≈80. That's the gap one transfer closes.

You called the ≈£1,630 drift unsure. That's the right call. A real month says whether it's a handful of things you'd happily cut, or spending you'd keep — right now it's just a number with no shape to it.

Checking a real month does two things. It swaps every ≈ for an actual figure — estimate and reality side by side. And the habits half of the picture is still completely empty: timing, patterns, what's truly recurring. Estimates can't see any of that. Only real transactions can.

Right now, I know you about 56%. Checking a real month is what takes that past 70%.

[CTA:start_statement_check]Check my numbers[/CTA]

— C.
